unitTitle: Organise work, study and future plans
title: Grammar: Near future: present of aller + infinitive
subtitle: A2 · Unit 5: Organise work, study and future plans

steps.title: Near future: present of aller + infinitive
steps.body: French often uses the present tense of aller plus an infinitive for an intention. The futur simple also expresses plans, schedules and predictions. These forms can overlap; the choice does not mean simply 'soon versus far away'.

steps.title: Keep the second verb in the infinitive: vais suivre, not vais suivrai.
Near future: present of aller + infinitive
steps.body:
• Use the present of aller with a second verb in the infinitive: nous allons vérifier; elle va participer.
• This pattern is common in everyday speech for a plan or intention. It can refer to a later date too; the date alone does not decide the tense.
• In your notes, change the subject in one plan: je vais suivre → nous allons suivre. Close the notes and rebuild the sentence.

steps.prompt: Choose the correct near-future form: Demain, nous ___ le dossier.
steps.explain: Use present allons plus the infinitive préparer.

steps.prompt: Complete: Cette semaine, elle ___ au test de niveau.
steps.explain: With elle, present aller is va, followed by the infinitive participer.
